title: Where the grant money went after two accessible ride services closed

beats.text: Two San Francisco wheelchair-accessible ride services shut down. What happened to their grant money?

visual.sub: One service ended early and another reached the end of its grant

beats.text: Tower stopped in September 2025. Fog City Access ran until its grant expired.

visual.kicker: One service ended early and another reached the end of its grant

beats.text: Agency staff cited late reports and insufficient ridership growth at Tower.

visual.kicker: Tower’s first two quarters showed trip growth, while staff raised reporting concerns

beats.text: Completed wheelchair-accessible requests rose from 15 to 134 across the first two quarters.
One payment appeared on Tower’s contract. Two more carried the same purchase order.

visual.kicker: Three payments on the same purchase order account for $765,958.98

beats.text: Together they left just over $730,000 available from the grant.

visual.heading: Tower’s funding
visual.context: Paid vouchers linked by purchase order

beats.text: Eleven payments on the Fog City grant left nearly $156,000.
The same vendor ran a separate service. Its payments belong to another contract.

visual.kicker: A separate Nomad contract would inflate the grant’s apparent cost

beats.text: The two grant balances add up to just under $886,000.

visual.kicker: The $885,984.57 difference reappeared in the next funding round

beats.text: The next competition listed exactly that amount from the earlier funding year.
The next question for riders is who received it and when replacement rides began.
Every source is linked in the case file below.
